description.narrative:
Sida is planning for support to the "National Environment Management Council", NEMC, in Tanzania. NEMC is Tanzania's equivalent of the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, SEPA. The support to NEMC is appraised and agreed separately from this contribution.
This contribution intends to enable the Swedish EPA to participate in the abovementioned project with NEMC.
The project with NEMC focus mainly on strengthening the environmental regulation in Tanzania, both at central and local level, by completing missing part of the Environmental Management Act and local by-laws. Capacity building is also included, mainly on environmental impact assessments for the environmental permit process.
The Swedish EPA will assist NEMC in drafting the new legislation and advise on the development of the environmental permit process.
A comprehensive and complete environment legislation framework is a prerequisite for managing possible environmental impacts of industrial activities, public services, business and activities in sectors such as tourism, fishing and agriculture.

Sida överväger stöd till "National Environment Management Council", NEMC, i Tanzania. NEMC är tanzanias motsvarighet till Naturvårdsverket. Stödet till NEMC bereds och avtalas separat från denna insats.
Denna insats avser Naturvårdsverkets medverkan i projektet med NEMC.
Projektet med NEMC avser komplettera ännu ofullständiga delar av tanzanias motsvarighet till miljöbalken, samt tillhörande förordningar och föreskrifter. Även insatser för att stärka kapaciteten hos NEMC är inkluderade, framför allt med fokus på miljökonsekvensbeskrivningar (MKB).
Naturvårdsverkets medverkan i projektet avser stöd till NEMC i arbetet med kompletterande regelverk och rådgivning kring MKB och tillståndsprocesser.
En fullgod miljölagstiftning är en förutsättning för att kunna hantera eventuella miljökonsekvenser av industriell verksamhet, kommunal service, företagsamhet, samt näringar såsom turism, fiske och lantbruk.

i) To establish the status of Environmental Management Act implementation
ii) To support formulation of additional regulations and guidelines for implementation of the environmental management act in Tanzania
iii) To support LGAs (local government authorities) in formulating environmental by-laws
iv) To enhance institutional capacity for effective implementation of EMA and for monitoring and reporting of imlementation of EMA in LGAs and MDAs (ministerial departments)
v) To enhance public awareness and private sector awareness and understanding on their roles and responsibilities in implementation of EMA.
The expected outcome is that the proposed project will lead to improved state of the environment in Tanzania, through effective coordination and implementation of the key environmental legislation across government at the central and local levels.

Due to the many challenges in the project as elaborated further on in the chapter below, the project managed to deliver some of its intended results. These are listed in bullets below.
- SwEPA conducted a factfinding mission to Tanzania which supported the production of a needs assessment that: o provided input to the overall methodology, work plan and measures suggested related to the assumed implementation of the main project to be implemented by VPO and NEMC. This informed the direction of the first strategic work plan of the overall project managed by VPO and NEMC.
- SwEPA evaluated and provided input to the Terms of Reference (ToR) produced by the VPO for developing a web-based system for processing applications.
- SwEPA provided overarching comments and recommendations to a plan produced by the VPO for development of an E-Waste Management system.
- SwEPA provided overarching comments and recommendations to a ToR produced by the VPO for preparing an Environmental Management Action Plan (EMAP) for Dodoma City.
- SwEPA provided brief response and comments to the proposed ToR for a National Waste Management Strategy.
- SwEPA contributed to evaluating selected parts of the Final Assessment Report produced by the VPO, that describes identified measures of what is needed to achieve implementation in various thematic sections of environmental legislation.
This support created a clearer understanding of the gaps that exist to reach a higher degree of implementation in these areas with the support of a Swedish perspective.
The project contributes to Sidas multifaceted support for partner countries to strengthen institutional capacity at the national, subnational, and local levels for implementing the Paris Agreement. Although from and throughout the initial phase it has been difficult for SEPA to provide the support they have agreed to provide the government of Tanzania (NEMC/VPO) since the GoT has not drawn on their expertise.
SwEPA opted to not extend the present agreement after dialogue with Sida. The previous extension of agreement was made with a clear understanding that any success in implementing the project would rely heavily on changed dynamics on the side of the collaborating partners in Tanzania. SwEPA sought to reignite the collaboration with the Tanzanian partners prior to and immediately after the extension of agreement.
Within the report there are some key lessons learned stated which are important to take into account in any future collaboration. SwEPA also have presence in the region through programme activities and staff which could enable any future prospects.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
